basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Anchors identifiers for subjects without owning their profile, account, credential or keys.
Records match and equivalence as assertions with evidence, not as automatic merges.
Keeps merge, split and supersession lineage so old identifiers still resolve.
Resolves identifiers purpose-bound rather than as open lookups.

may: Resolve an identifier for a stated purpose and return the minimum attributes.
Propose duplicate candidates with match evidence.
Map identifiers to a federated namespace with lineage.
Report assurance levels attached to a registration.
mustNot: Merge two entries on name similarity or match score alone.
Treat a successful lookup as authentication or authorization.
Reassign a retired identifier to a new subject.
Expose resolution results beyond the stated purpose.
Delete entries that legal retention rules require to keep.
requiresHuman: Handling a subject rights request such as erasure or correction.

considerations: Wrong merges can attach one person's records to another, with serious consequences.
Central registers enable tracking; purpose limitation and minimisation protect subjects.
People must be able to correct identity errors that block their access to services.

items: A register entry has a namespace, an identifier, a subject type, a registration authority and a lifecycle state.
It is confused with the subject profile, an account, a credential or a master data record.
Identity theft through weak registration evidence.
Broken references when identifiers are reused or not superseded properly.
